name: frontend-design-pro
description: Machine-enforced frontend UI/UX skill pack for AI agents. Registry + lazy loading: 19 auto-routing skills, 8 core files, 119 references (436,039 tokens of on-demand depth), 55 examples, 61 machine-enforced constraints, 11 release-blocking gates. A typical request loads 6,037–7,950 tokens, not 436,039. Setup docs for 6 agent surfaces (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, OpenAI API, Copilot, Gemini), native one-line install via setup.sh/setup.ps1 for 14 adapters (10 automatic, 4 manual), and two real, runnable Next.js demo apps.
author: krishnamodi241@gmail.com

stats.ci_constraints_detail: 61 checks across 61 distinct IDs (17 parser AST + 44 regex)

changelog.14.14.1: The marketplace route was documented at length and never once run. Measured against v14.14.0 with `claude plugin marketplace add`, the plugin manifest registers TWENTY skills, not one: all 19 sub-skills as peers plus the root router, ~1,991 tokens always-on, which is the sum of twenty descriptions rather than the 2,149-token registry. That is exactly the inversion .claude-plugin/README.md said "./skills/" would cause, arriving through "./". The mechanism, measured against a five-case fixture rather than inferred: skill discovery is exactly one directory level beneath a top-level skills/ at the plugin root, and it is unconditional — the manifest field only ever adds paths, it cannot subtract. "skills": [] and "skills": ["./SKILL.md"] both still register the nineteen and both drop the router, so ["./"] stays as the least-bad value. The fix is structural — the directory literally named skills/ must not exist at the plugin root, and 130 files reference it — so it is recorded with its evidence rather than taken, and no marketplace listing should be submitted until it is resolved. This release exists so the shipped archive stops asserting the disproved claim. Also corrects three stale claims: CONTRIBUTING.md said the renderer checks are not in CI (demo-renderer runs them), CONTRIBUTING.md and .claude-plugin/README.md both undercounted the version-bump locations, and tools/screenshots/README.md said demo/showcase is excluded from visual regression when it has been included since the capture began freezing the seed. No content figure moved.

The showcase also gained the skip link it had been missing, so demo/ passes 4/4 projects at 44/44 with nothing waived, up from 3/4 with a waiver. Gate 11's SCAN gained .claude-plugin/*.md, which had never been read and was claiming a 2,088-token registry against a real 2,149; 0 drifts over 153 claim surfaces now. home/'s hero corpus was rebuilt as a ring that can actually be seen. No content figure moved: 19 skills, 8 core files, 119 references, 61 constraints, 11 release-blocking gates.
changelog.14.13.0: Two release-blocking checks that were not actually checking, and a landing page rebuilt around the one thing it had never shown. prose_paths() in Stage 3 now reads every backticked path the pack writes in prose and fails the build on a dead one; the four addressing forms this repo uses were understood by nothing before it, and the first run found 15 dead pointers, some of which had shipped for eleven releases. The pre-commit guard matched a list of porcelain spellings and so saw 3 of the 11 dirty states git can report, including a file staged and then edited again, which is green in git status while the commit carries only the older half; it matches the worktree column now and npm run hooks:test asserts all 11 in both directions. Every authored-path check was case-sensitive where it meant to be case-insensitive, Gate 7c was repaired, and SLOP-04's bypass is closed. home/ gained renderer checks in CI: the home-renderer job runs pages:verify, so the landing page's axe, hydration, overflow and reduced-motion coverage is blocking rather than something someone remembers to run, and it earned itself immediately by catching a 12-violation contrast regression before it shipped. On the page itself: the accent moved off terracotta to a measured marine, oklch(50.5% 0.088 225), chosen on an OKLab delta-E matrix rather than on taste, because two opposing WCAG floors leave a lightness window about four points wide at every hue and contrast therefore cannot discriminate between viable candidates. The hero was a WebGL object extruded from the reference corpus that rendered as an anonymous grey brick and was not legible as the corpus at all; the same data is drawn flat now, one mark per reference with width proportional to that file's real token count, wrapping like a page of set type, one mark lit for the single reference a request would load. That took three, a 388-line harness whose docblock described deleted features, and the page's only documented exception to its own interaction tier out with it. The showcase is a coverflow carousel on a native scroll-snap track, no Swiper and no second animation runtime. Two defects that no gate could see were found by walking the rendered page: two of the fourteen adapter marks rendered at 1.000:1 on the inverted install section, rgb(2,1,1) on rgb(1,1,3), because one icon drew in currentColor and inherited the page's near-black ink, and axe has no contrast rule for a decorative aria-hidden graphic. References moved 117 to 119 via the emilkowalski/skills and ibelick/ui-skills ingestion. Registry, skills, core files, constraints and gates all unchanged.

changelog.14.11.5: New depth on design-research, not a new skill. It now runs a Phase 0 social-and-trend pass before the gallery step: when the user points at a community rather than a page ("what's trending in X design", "what are people building for Y", "what does the community think of Z pattern"), it pulls an engagement-ranked signal, converts it into the same typed constraints a browsed page produces, and hands off to the build skill. Two optional external tools cover that pass: last30days (parallel search across Reddit/X/YouTube/HN/GitHub/Polymarket, scored by real engagement, duplicate stories merged, cited brief) and agent-reach (a read/search capability layer over Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu, RSS and Exa semantic search, with primary-to-backup backend fallback). Neither is a dependency of design-research or any skill, and neither is vendored: they are detected via `agent-reach doctor` / `last30days --preflight`, preferred for time-sensitive or platform-specific or engagement-ranked questions when healthy, and degraded silently to plain web_search with no error and no install prompt when absent, the same posture the constraint suites already take toward a missing TypeScript compiler. New references/social-signal-research.md (167 lines) carries the tool detail, three worked examples and the zero/one/both degrade matrix, cited in design-research's Reference Index. core/agent-behavior.md gains one universal paragraph: prefer a configured research tool over an unqualified web_search for time-sensitive or community-sentiment questions, never block on absence. design-research's When-to-Use triggers and the root registry keyword cell gained the community phrasings. Figures: references 111 to 112, reference depth 402,592 to 404,917 tokens, registry 2,112 to 2,126 tokens from the added keywords, per-request band 6,000-7,599 to 6,014-7,927; design-research remains the heaviest skill and now sits 73 tokens under the Gate 8a ceiling. 11/11 gates green, 0 figure drift.
changelog.14.11.4: Two fixes, both verified by running the check, not by reading it. SLOP-04 was structurally inert: the corpus's own deliberate anti-example for it (bad-generic.tsx) passed the check outright, because the two dollar-figures it named as banned matched its own organic-evidence pattern, a trailing word-boundary after percent often failed to anchor, and the bare comma-figure shape the anti-example and landing-pages's own reference doc actually use was never in the ban list. Built a standalone test harness and ran every candidate fix against all 137 example files before touching the real script. Fixed the comma/dollar half: wrapped the check in _uncommented() so an illustrative JSDoc comment can no longer supply its own escape hatch, widened the ban to bare 10,000/100,000 with an optional plus, and excluded those two literals from the organic-evidence pattern so they can no longer satisfy their own ban. Verified zero new false positives across the full corpus and that the anti-example now fails SLOP-04 specifically. Left the percent half unfixed on purpose: oklch lightness values, calc() expressions, Tailwind arbitrary values and inline width/height percentages are genuine, frequent, legitimate code in this corpus, and every percent-aware fix attempted produced a false positive a comma-only check does not; the description now states the narrower, accurate coverage instead of overclaiming, same move as the prior release's GAP-2 fix applied to the one half of the claim that turned out to be actually fixable. Second, a real and previously confirmed-empty coverage gap: platform had nothing for extension UI, VS Code webviews or browser extension popups, even though this pack's other platform surfaces are all covered. Researched current guidance from VS Code's own UX Guidelines and Webview API docs and Chrome's Manifest V3 documentation. Both surfaces share constraints nothing else in this pack assumes: a host-imposed theme rather than the app's own, a fixed small viewport, and a CSP that forbids several patterns this pack otherwise treats as normal, most notably any CSS-in-JS approach that injects style tags at runtime. New references/extension-ui.md covers VS Code theming via its CSS custom properties and body theme classes, the Webview UI Toolkit, postMessage host communication and nonce-based CSP, plus MV3 popup constraints: roughly 400px width, default CSP, options-page-owns-persisted-settings, and full keyboard/focus discipline. Reference depth grew 1,388 tokens to 373,600; reference count grew by one file to 105. Registry and per-request band unchanged. 11/11 gates green, 0 figure drift.
changelog.14.11.3: Second half of the same web-research pass, closing a confirmed-empty coverage gap the earlier survey flagged and deliberately deferred rather than rushed into the previous release. AI-generated image handling was previously absent everywhere in the pack, confirmed zero mentions across every reference file before anything was written. Platform already covered long-running-work status generically and web-interface covered image CLS, but neither addressed what is specific to on-demand generation: a moderation rejection needs a different fix than a network failure and the two are easy to collapse into one error state, alt text cannot be authored up front since there is no ground truth until the image exists and must never default to the prompt text, and a regenerate affordance is not optional polish when unpredictability is the feature. Added as a new pattern in platform's SKILL.md, composing the existing rules rather than duplicating them, no new core rule or reference file. Verified rather than changed: browser-extension and VS Code extension UI remain genuinely uncovered and left open as their own scoped pass rather than a rushed addition here. Registry, band and every skill's token budget unchanged. 11/11 gates green, 0 figure drift.

changelog.14.11.1: A 12-fresh-agent behavioral audit, genuinely isolated agents with zero conversation history run against SKILL.md as an installed skill, found 4 documentation defects, no engineering failures. The anti-slop wall banned gradient fills on large headings absolutely while TYP-03, the machine-enforced rule, calls the same pattern legitimate on a display heading; the wall now matches TYP-03's scope, banned on body text only, which also keeps a claim elsewhere in the docs true about how this pack's own gradient-text rule differs from a named competitor's. SLOP-04 claimed to catch round-number placeholder data but its own regex lets a value like $100,000 pass as organic; rather than widen the regex unchecked against the gold corpus, its description now states the narrower coverage it actually has, with the regex fix left as a follow-up. Platform owned responsive-on-mobile routing but its Core Rules were entirely native and PWA content with nothing about web breakpoints; it gained a real rule covering min-width queries, grid stacking, table scrolling and a viewport test matrix. agent-behavior.md's four principles had no rule protecting a concern the user names as primary over feature work; a fifth principle now requires implementing and verifying that concern first and saying so in the plan. Also verified rather than rewritten: a prior plan named five reference files as still owed from an earlier ingestion sprint, and the changelog already showed each one closed as covered elsewhere in the pack or deliberately rejected, so nothing new was written. changelog.14.10.1: Gate 11 could not read the sentence "SKILL.md is 2,018 tokens". The registry anchor required the filename in backticks, or "always"/"registry" within thirty characters of the same sentence — docs prose backticks a filename, prose written for strangers does not. All three tracked launch documents carried the superseded router size in live present-tense prose while the gate reported 0 drift over 85 surfaces. Two more forms of the same defect sat beside it: RANGE only matched a dashed pair, so "5,665 to 7,266 tokens" was not a range; and the band split across two sentences as "the heaviest … the lightest …" matched nothing at all. 20 stale figures, none visible in a green run. LAUNCH_FINAL.md's file-wide REGISTRY exemption turned out to be silencing four live claims rather than the historical passage its stated reason named — that passage never matched the pattern. The exemption is gone, replaced by scoped figures:historical markers — and README.md already used those markers in three places for exactly this purpose, so the scoped tool was established practice in the same repo and the blanket got reached for anyway. Two shipped manifests were outside the scan entirely: metadata.json's prose description claimed 94 references and 10 gates against the 101 and 11 its own stats block already recorded, and plugin.json — what a marketplace listing renders — claimed 96. New figure_pattern_test.py holds 20 prose fixtures over 5 figures, asserting in both directions, blocking in the chain and not a twelfth gate. Its negative cases caught the widened anchor reading the per-skill router range out of skills/{id}/SKILL.md as if it were the registry, which would have failed two correct tables.
changelog.14.10.0: The pack was written touch-first and never said what changes when the pointer is precise. platform carried nine references — mobile, React Native, email, i18n, SEO, Stripe, AI SDK and two agent-ops files — and nothing about desktop; references/desktop-patterns.md closes it. The value is not the topic but that three of our own rules read differently there and the pack had never said so. Target size: we enforce 44x44 everywhere, but on a pointer-only surface the WCAG AA floor is 24x24 CSS px, and the file says which to pick and why. Spacing: the 4pt scale is unchanged, desktop density is a choice of step within it (8 rather than 4), not a different scale. Hover: an enhancement on touch, the primary affordance on desktop, where a pointer resting on a control with no feedback reads as broken. It also names a constraint the mobile-first material never states — a desktop app is stared at for hours, so motion is judged on its hundredth repetition rather than its first. Reconciling that against core/accessibility-baseline.md found it claiming 'Targets >=44x44px with >=24px spacing (2.5.8)', which attributes a AAA number to an AA criterion: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is AA and asks for 24x24, while 44x44 is 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), which is AAA. The 44px rule itself is right and unchanged, a deliberate house rule stricter than AA; what was wrong was the citation behind it, in one of the eight files loaded on every matched request. No gate reads a specification number and none can — this was found by ingesting a source that disagreed. Two smaller additions: Skiper UI joins shadcn-ecosystem.md as the only catalogue entry with a paid tier and a client-rendered listing that returns a loading shell to anything that fetches rather than browses it; and brand-extraction.md gains a section on sourcing a palette from something that is not a brand, since it covered brands with a published palette and had nothing for 'make it feel like a Vermeer' — paintings, film grades and terminal themes behave differently and carry different rights, and a palette derived from a work must be labelled an evocation rather than a reproduction. Sources surveyed and deliberately not used: obra/superpowers and gsd-build/get-shit-done are software-development methodology, real quality but wrong domain, and the parts that do apply are already in agent-ops/references/skill-packaging.md; theme-factory-addon's 100 themes duplicate our 161 OKLCH palettes in hex, so only its method was taken; genjutsu's SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose skills are out of scope for a React and web pack. Correction to an earlier audit: JuliusBrussee/caveman was reported as an unattributed source and is not — metadata.json lists the repository in sources and the 10.13.0 entry names it; the audit never checked the sources array. Gate count unchanged at 11. References 96 to 97; depth 337,392 to 339,838 tokens; a request now costs 5,865-7,465.
changelog.14.9.0: Eight of the ten references our own gold examples cite did not exist, and the pack ships a marketplace manifest for the first time. Six good-*.tsx open with a // Source doctrine: line naming the references their rules come from; ten are named across those six files and two resolved. phosphor.md, openui.md, aceternity.md, component-registry.md, interaction-patterns.md, visual-hierarchy.md, gestalt.md and component-api.md were each planned in an ingestion batch that ran out of context budget before the file was written — the comment shipped, the reference never did. No gate could see it: Stage 3 path integrity reads BACKTICKED `references/*.md` paths inside skills/*/SKILL.md, and these are unbackticked comments in .tsx, so eight dead pointers survived every green build for as long as the examples have existed. Stage 3 now also walks skills/*/examples/*.tsx, reads the doctrine header and resolves each path against the skill directory; it was verified to FAIL before it was trusted, naming all eight against the tree at d034fb7, the same standard Gate 6 was held to. It extends Stage 3 rather than becoming Gate 12 for the reason markdown_links() gives directly above it. Each comment is repointed at the reference that actually carries its doctrine, verified line by line: the Gestalt-proximity rule lands on laws-of-ux.md, which states Von Restorff as 'exactly one primary CTA per view'; the spotlight card lands on react-bits.md, whose wrapper-effects section names the effect. The §6-7 in good-composition-patterns.tsx was wrong twice over — those sections are Performance and Error Boundaries; compound components are §1. The eight missing files are NOT written here; that is 8 new references, 8 Reference Index rows and a reference_files move, and it is the next minor's work. Distribution: .claude-plugin/ ships. Every install route began with a manual step while a marketplace entry is a command — the most plausible explanation for distribution at zero. The manifest was blocked for three research batches on the fear that a skills array would make a host load all nineteen. Surveying microsoft/agent-skills retired it: nobody enumerates, and azure-sdk-python ships 40 SKILL.md behind one directory pointer. But their pointer is not ours and copying it would have been the bug — behind Microsoft's ./skills/ are the skills they want registered, behind ours are the nineteen the router exists to hide, so "skills": ["./skills/"] would register all nineteen as peers, the --full-depth inversion docs/INSTALL.md tells people never to trigger. We ship "skills": ["./"], the root that holds the router, and .claude-plugin/README.md records why since JSON carries no comments. This is a declaration, not a proof: nothing surveyed documents what a host does on load. Committing the file publishes nothing, so the obligation is to add the marketplace locally, confirm ONE skill registers rather than nineteen, and withdraw the file if it is nineteen. version in plugin.json is the fourth place the version lives; .claude-plugin/ had to join the version-leak allowlist for it to exist, verified as a build-breaker rather than assumed since writing the file first failed Stage 1 on .claude-plugin/plugin.json:4. An allowlisted path is one nothing checks, so bump_patch() rewrites it and Gate 2 asserts it matches metadata.json, that assertion also confirmed to fire before it was trusted. Gate count unchanged at 11. No constraint, figure or token budget moved.
changelog.14.8.1: The archive told people to read files it did not contain. 22 shipped files carried 137 references to docs/*.md and the archive had no docs/ directory at all — including all 14 install/*/README.md per-agent setup guides and the last line setup.sh prints, on the gated-archive route the README recommends for the verified artifact. It had been broken for the pack's entire life and was found by doing the thing nobody had done: downloading a published release into a clean directory and following its own instructions. Fixed three ways. The 13 consumer-facing docs (compatibility matrix, install, usage, architecture, FAQ, testing, demo prompts, and the six per-host setup guides) now ship at docs/ in the archive, ~89 KB against ~1.9 MB — split by audience, not size, because a consumer needs their host's setup guide and does not need the freeze policy or the review protocol. docs/CHANGELOG.md references are repointed to _meta/CHANGELOG.md, where that file actually ships. Anything still unshippable is rewritten to an absolute URL pinned to the tag it shipped under, not to main: an archive is a snapshot, and pointing a v14.x reader at today's main is how a document starts lying. _meta/CHANGELOG.md is exempt from rewriting, being the historical record. Stage 6 now asserts that every docs/ path cited by a shipped file resolves inside the archive, using the same two link shapes and the same exclusions as the rewriter so the check and the fix cannot disagree. No constraint, gate count or figure changed.
changelog.14.8.0: Gate 11 — the figure gate. CLAUDE.md named the same defect as this repo's worst for several releases: no gate validates prose, so counts and token figures hardcoded across ~30 documents go stale silently. Every gate read code; the thing that kept breaking was arithmetic in markdown, defended only by remembering to sweep a list of files. scripts/check_figures.py recomputes every figure from the filesystem — never from metadata.json, which it audits instead — and fails the build on any document that disagrees. Figures are matched by shape and context rather than against a list of known-stale literals, so the NEXT drift is caught and not only this one. Token counts are LF-normalised: a gate whose whole job is arithmetic cannot have a platform-dependent answer. Four checks: anchored figures, stated deltas that must subtract correctly, metadata.json against the tree, and metadata's changelog against docs/CHANGELOG.md. First run: 64 drifts. The per-request band was wrong in 17 live files, two shipped inside the archive — AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md told an agent its own budget was 5,511-7,112 when it was 5,665-7,266; a second, rounder band (5,000-6,300) circulated in five more, already disagreeing with the first before either went stale. ARCHITECTURE.md's per-skill budget table was wrong in all 19 rows and had been hand-re-derived TWICE in the preceding release by commits whose messages read 're-derive every figure' — stale again the moment that release shipped, which is the argument for the gate rather than a footnote to it. Three documents claimed two skills grew the registry by 103 tokens between endpoints that subtract to 107 and 123; only docs/CHANGELOG.md kept the self-consistent original, because CLAUDE.md forbids rewriting it. Also: 'Nine named gates' above a ten-row table, gates 2 and 8 reporting 17/17 for 19 skills, gate 5 reporting 39/39 for 45 golds, path integrity claiming 87 cited references against 95, GEMINI_SETUP's 'the 17 routers', audit-report.html's 56 constraints. And the check that pays for itself immediately: the preceding release shipped with no metadata changelog entry at all, restored here. Exemptions carry a written reason; historical records are exempt wholesale; release notes that must name a superseded figure use a marked region that stays visible in the diff, and a marker without a reason or without a close is itself a finding. What it cannot see: figures spelled as words, and documents outside its SCAN list. Gates 10 -> 11.
changelog.14.7.4: Two taste defects found by the research layer, both in reference prose no gate reads for correctness, and both contradictions where the pack stated a rule and shipped code breaking it in the same skill. The reduced-motion snippet in animation-framework.md and animation-recipes.md prescribed `* { animation: none !important }`, which removes the animation so animationend and transitionend never fire — any component gating unmount or cleanup on those events hangs forever, for exactly the users who asked for less motion. Replaced with the near-zero-duration form. h-screen was banned in prose three times and shipped in code five: RES-03 keys on the literal min-h-screen, so a bare h-screen matched nothing. Fixed in scroll-experience.md (x2), spline.md, brand-core.md and brand-design-systems.md, using h-[100svh] for the two scroll-driven containers where dvh reflows mid-scroll. Entry reconstructed from docs/CHANGELOG.md in 14.8.0: the release shipped without one, and nothing compared the two records until Gate 11.
changelog.14.7.3: Competitor survey widened from four packs to eight, and metadata.json's changelog restored. Packs read at source: impeccable, ui-ux-pro-max-skill, anthropics/skills frontend-design, taste-skill, rohitg00/awesome-claude-design, vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines, emilkowalski/skill. The question is narrow and falsifiable — does the project run its own design rules over its own shipped guidance? Two of eight enforce design rules mechanically; one of those two gates its own material. The four added in this pass have zero CI workflows and zero test files between them. Correction owed to impeccable: earlier notes here described its detectors as pointing outward as though it were untested. It is not — 14 test targets including detector, framework, e2e and live-agent suites, more test infrastructure than this pack has. It tests that its detector WORKS; it does not point that detector at skill/reference/*.md. changelog.14.7.1: Correction. v14.7.0 said its three new constraints covered defects "nobody checks" and that no competing pack enforced them. That was asserted, not verified. Checked against source: impeccable DOES ship a gradient-text detector firing on background-clip:text plus a gradient, so the claim was wrong for TYP-03 — though impeccable's fires unconditionally, including on display headings where the effect is legitimate, while TYP-03 is scoped to body-sized text. changelog.14.7.0: Three constraints for defects the field ships and nobody checks, found by sweeping both suites for gaps rather than by adding rules that sounded good. A11Y-06: outline-none with no focus indicator. A11Y-02 (AST) already checked that a focus-visible class sits on an interactive element — it catches the ring being in the wrong PLACE and cannot catch it being removed and replaced with nothing, which is the far commoner defect. Either focus: or focus-visible: satisfies the rule; a focus-trapped dialog container is the one legitimate bare outline-none and takes a documented exemption. TYP-03: bg-clip-text on body-sized text. Legitimate on a display heading; on prose it sets the computed colour to transparent, which destroys contrast and silently defeats every contrast checker, because the ratio is measured against a colour no reader sees. FORM-01: an input, textarea or select carrying text-sm (14px) or text-xs (12px). Below 16px iOS Safari zooms the viewport on focus and does not zoom back — invisible on desktop, universal on iPhone. All three are ban-shaped, so all three were added to Gate 10's FRAGMENT_SAFE set and run over the whole reference corpus, not only the examples. They immediately found 22 real defects in this pack's own shipped material: 11 in gold examples (good-rhf, good-checkout, good-react19, good-performance-patterns, good-image-palette, good-react-native) and 11 in references, including five in auth-patterns.md — the file that teaches agents how to build sign-in forms. Every one is fixed. Constraints 56 → 59 (17 parser AST + 42 regex). Gate 10 now applies 19 ban-shaped constraints, up from 16.
